title: Metabolic Processes
standard_text: Energy and ATP; the stages of aerobic cellular respiration (glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, the electron transport chain and chemiosmosis); anaerobic respiration and fermentation; and the light-dependent and light-independent reactions of photosynthesis. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 11 and 12: Science (2008), Biology, Grade 12, University Preparation (SBI4U), Strand C: Metabolic Processes)
meta_desc: Free Grade 12 Biology (SBI4U) worksheets on metabolic processes: ATP, glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, the electron transport chain, fermentation, and the light reactions and Calvin cycle of photosynthesis. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Cellular respiration releases energy from glucose; photosynthesis stores it.
key_sub: Glycolysis → Krebs cycle → electron transport chain.
body_html:
How to think about it

Aerobic respiration: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + energy (about 36 ATP). Glycolysis in the cytoplasm splits glucose into two pyruvate (net 2 ATP). In the mitochondria, the Krebs cycle releases CO₂ and loads NADH and FADH₂; the electron transport chain pumps H⁺ ions, and ATP synthase makes most of the ATP. Oxygen is the final electron acceptor.

Without oxygen, cells use fermentation (lactate in muscles, ethanol and CO₂ in yeast) and make only 2 ATP per glucose. Photosynthesis: the light reactions in the thylakoids split water, release O₂ and make ATP and NADPH; the Calvin cycle in the stroma uses them to fix CO₂ into sugar.

Example

Where does glycolysis happen?

It is the first stage and does not need mitochondria.

Answer: in the cytoplasm

Example

What is the role of oxygen in respiration?

It accepts electrons at the end of the chain.

Answer: final electron acceptor, forming water

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants do not respire: plant cells respire all the time.
  • Saying the oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from CO₂: it comes from water.
  • Thinking fermentation makes as much ATP as aerobic respiration.

faq.q: Why is the electron transport chain important?
faq.a: It makes most of the ATP by pumping H⁺ ions that then flow back through ATP synthase.

items.q: Fermentation makes 2 ATP per glucose. How many ATP come from 50 glucose molecules?

Equation: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> + 6O<sub>2</sub> → 6CO<sub>2</sub> + 6H<sub>2</sub>O + energy (ATP). A cell breaks down 35 glucose molecules completely. How many CO<sub>2</sub> molecules are released?
items.e: 6 per glucose: 6 × 35 = 210.

items.q: Where is the electron transfer chain?
items.e: Folding into cristae gives a large surface area.

items.q: How many more ATP does aerobic respiration (about 36 per glucose) make than fermentation (2 per glucose) from 25 glucose molecules?

Equation: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> + 6O<sub>2</sub> → 6CO<sub>2</sub> + 6H<sub>2</sub>O + energy (ATP). A cell breaks down 5 glucose molecules completely. How many O<sub>2</sub> molecules are used?
items.e: 6 per glucose: 6 × 5 = 30.

items.q: An organism takes in 30 mL of oxygen and gives out 22 mL of carbon dioxide. Calculate the respiratory quotient.
items.e: RQ = CO₂ given out ÷ O₂ taken in = 0.733 (1.0 for carbohydrate, about 0.7 for lipid, about 0.9 for protein).

items.q: How many more ATP does aerobic respiration (about 36 per glucose) make than fermentation (2 per glucose) from 3 glucose molecules?
What is the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration?
items.e: Oxygen combines with electrons and protons to form water.

items.q: Equation: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> + 6O<sub>2</sub> → 6CO<sub>2</sub> + 6H<sub>2</sub>O + energy (ATP). A cell breaks down 4 glucose molecules completely. How many O<sub>2</sub> molecules are used?
items.e: 6 per glucose: 6 × 4 = 24.

items.q: What does ATP synthase do?
c: uses the flow of protons to make ATP from ADP and Pᵢ
items.e: Found in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

items.q: Fermentation makes 2 ATP per glucose. How many ATP come from 3 glucose molecules?

items.e: 6 per glucose: 6 × 34 = 204.

items.q: What are cristae?
c: folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane
items.e: They give a large surface area for the electron transfer chain.

items.q: How many more ATP does aerobic respiration (about 36 per glucose) make than fermentation (2 per glucose) from 2 glucose molecules?
What is produced in anaerobic respiration in yeast?
items.e: This is alcoholic fermentation.

items.q: What is the role of NAD in respiration?
c: it carries hydrogen (protons and electrons) to the electron transfer chain
items.e: It is reduced in glycolysis, the link reaction and the Krebs cycle.

items.q: Aerobic respiration makes about 36 ATP per glucose. About how many ATP come from 2 glucose molecules?

Equation: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> + 6O<sub>2</sub> → 6CO<sub>2</sub> + 6H<sub>2</sub>O + energy (ATP). A cell breaks down 14 glucose molecules completely. How many O<sub>2</sub> molecules are used?
items.e: 6 per glucose: 6 × 14 = 84.

items.q: Fermentation makes 2 ATP per glucose. How many ATP come from 5 glucose molecules?

items.e: 6 per glucose: 6 × 40 = 240.

items.q: What is the net gain of ATP when 7 molecules of glucose are broken down by glycolysis alone?
items.e: Net 2 ATP per glucose (4 made, 2 used): 14 ATP.

items.q: Which is used in respiration if carbohydrates run out?
items.e: Fats enter as acetyl CoA, proteins as amino acids.

items.q: Which organism makes ethanol and CO₂ by fermentation?
items.e: Used in making bread and alcohol.

items.q: How many molecules of CO₂ are released in the complete aerobic respiration of 5 molecules of glucose?
items.e: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O: 30.

items.q: What is the net gain of ATP when 2 molecules of glucose are broken down by glycolysis alone?
items.e: Net 2 ATP per glucose (4 made, 2 used): 4 ATP.

items.q: How many turns of the Krebs cycle are needed to oxidize 4 molecules of glucose completely?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 acetyl CoA, so 2 turns: 8.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 5 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 5 = 10.

items.q: What is the end product of glycolysis?
items.e: Glucose → 2 pyruvic acid.

items.q: Where in the cell does the Krebs cycle take place?
items.e: The Krebs cycle: the mitochondrial matrix.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 8 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 8 = 16.

items.q: How many molecules of CO₂ are released in the complete aerobic respiration of 1 molecule of glucose?
items.e: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O: 6.

items.q: How many molecules of CO₂ are released in the complete aerobic respiration of 4 molecules of glucose?
items.e: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O: 24.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 10 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 10 = 20.

items.q: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are formed from 4 molecules of glucose in glycolysis?
items.e: Each glucose gives 2 pyruvic acid: 2 × 4 = 8.

items.q: What is the first product of the Krebs cycle?
items.e: Acetyl CoA + oxaloacetic acid → citric acid.

items.q: What happens in human muscles during heavy exercise when oxygen is short?
c: pyruvic acid is reduced to lactic acid
items.e: This causes fatigue.

items.q: What is the net gain of ATP from glycolysis of one glucose?
items.e: 4 are made but 2 are used.

items.q: What is the net gain of ATP when 1 molecule of glucose is broken down by glycolysis alone?
items.e: Net 2 ATP per glucose (4 made, 2 used): 2 ATP.

items.q: Which enzyme makes ATP in the inner mitochondrial membrane?
items.e: Protons flow through it.

items.q: Where in the cell does fermentation take place?
items.e: Fermentation: the cytoplasm, without oxygen.

items.q: Which photosystem is used in cyclic photophosphorylation?

items.e: It makes ATP but no NADPH or O₂.

items.q: Why do C₄ plants show almost no photorespiration?

items.e: So RuBisCO works as a carboxylase.

items.e: Reduced NADP is used to reduce GP.

items.q: What happens to glycerate 3-phosphate (GP) in the Calvin cycle?

items.e: Some triose phosphate makes glucose; most regenerates RuBP.

items.q: How is ATP made in the light-dependent reaction?
